data.text:
Sweta Maurya And Another vs State Of Up And 7 Others on 6 
March, 2024 
Author: Renu Agarwal
Bench: Renu Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
? Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:40791
Court No. - 81 
Case :- Writ - C No. - 7247 of 2024
Petitioner :- Sweta Maurya And Another
Respondent :- State Of Up And 7 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Gaurav Tripathi,Praveen Kumar Singh 
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Mrs. Renu Agarwal,J.
1. Instant writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution has been filed by the petitioners with
prayer for issuing writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents not
to interfere in the peaceful living of the petitioners and also to command the respondent No. 1 and 2
to send the petitioner to Women and Children's Shelter Home till she attains majority. 
2.  It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners being resident of nearby village situated at very short distance used to meet everyday and when the news of their meeting broke out, the father of the petitioner No. 1 got furated and tried to solemnize marriage of the petitioner No. 1 with someone else. The petitioner No. 1 is aged about 17 years 6 months and 20 Sweta Maurya And Another vs State Of Up And 7 Others on 6 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167520626/
1 days. The petitioner No. 2 though an adult is not of marriageable age. Parents of petitioner No. 1 tried to solemnize her marriage forcibly with someone, the petitioner No. 1 opposed the marriage. 
Thereafter the father, brothers and sister of the petitioner No. 1 confined the petitioner No. 1 in a room and refused to give her food and water and threatened the petitioner No. 1 of life. On 22.02.2024 petitioner No. 1 ran away from her parental house and tried to take refuge with petitioner No. 2. When the petitioner No. 2 has not received any help from his parents, he came in contact with lawyers in Tehsil Sakaldiha District Chandauli, whereupon they were directed to seek protection of the Court. 
3. The petitioners came to Allahabad to seek the protection from this Court and tried to meet District Magistrate and apprise him of the situation but it was of no use and District Magistrate has not given any receiving of the application. The petitioner No. 1 tried to convince her father over phone but she was given threat by her father, therefore the present petition has been filed. 
4. Learned Standing Counsel submitted that petitioner No. 1 is a minor and not of marriageable age. 
Petitioner No. 2 though a major is not of marriageable age as prescribed under law. They have neither claimed that they are married nor they are living in relationship, this Court has no jurisdiction to try the matter of illegal detention, hence, this Court cannot grant any relief in this matter. 
5. I have heard rival submissions and perused the record. 
6. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioner passed on to this Court order passed by Division Bench of this Court in the case of Jyoti and 5 others Vs. State of U.P. and 5 others Writ C No. 11275 of 2019 and submitted that in this case also the petitioner was minor and therefore, she was directed by the Division Bench of this Court to be kept in Asha Jyoti Kendra,
Prayagraj and protection is given for safety of girl till she attains the age of majority. Ossification test of petitioner was also directed and she was found major on the date of order and Division Bench of this Court provided protection to the petitioners.
7. The facts of Writ C No. 11275 of 2019 goes to show that the petitioner Jyoti was miner and her father solemnized her marriage with respondent No. 3 in that case and she instead of refuting her marriage after attaining majority, took shelter of the Court stating that she do not want to reside with respondent No. 3, therefore, the Court granted her interim protection so that she can be protected from respondent No. 3 her husband and the facts of the case of Jyoti (supra) are not the same as in the present case. In the present case, both the petitioners are not of marriageable age and petitioner No. 1 is not major yet. There is no proof on record to show that she was detained by her father, brother and sister. There is no proof of the fact that petitioners have any relationship as married couple or as couple in relationship. Civil Misc. Stay Application No. 1 of 2024 is also moved by the petitioner seeking prayer to issue ad interim mandamus commanding the respondent not to take any coercive action against the petitioners and to give her custody to Women and Children Shelter Home till she attains majority. The prayer for interim relief is not in consonance with prayer in the writ petition . 
Sweta Maurya And Another vs State Of Up And 7 Others on 6 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167520626/
2 8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner No. 2 is added as the next friend and drew my attention towards order 22. Petitioner No. 2 admittedly is not a next friend appointed by any court under the provisions of Guardians and Wards Act nor is he nominated by the Court in any way, therefore the petitioner No. 2 has no locus standi to file a petition as next friend. In this petition the petitioner No. 2 is not the next friend, hence, petitioner No. 2 has no locus standi as married couple or couple in relationship. This Court has no jurisdiction to adjudicate upon. 
9. In view of the above submission this writ petition is dismissed. However, liberty is given to the petitioner to avail appropriate remedy as available in law. 
(Renu Agarwal,J.) Order Date :- 6.3.2024 Nadeem  Sweta Maurya And Another vs State Of Up And 7 Others on 6 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167520626/
